question.text: A PMS portfolio was worth Rs. 1,00,000 at the start of a year and Rs. 1,20,000 at year-end, with Rs. 5,000 dividend received during the year. What is the Holding Period Return (HPR)?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** HPR = (I + (E − B)) / B = (5000 + (1,20,000 − 1,00,000)) / 1,00,000 = 25,000 / 1,00,000 = 25%. **The Trap:** 20% is the price-only return; 30% double-counts; 15% forgets price appreciation. **Cross-Exam Context:** V-A, X-A, XV all test HPR; XXI-B expects fluency. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Always clarify if client wants 'total return' (includes distributions) or 'capital-only return' — the gap can exceed 100 bps annually.
